security_audit.summary: This skill is a static Markdown reference guide for designing REST and GraphQL APIs. All 36 static findings are false positives: the flagged patterns are Markdown code fences misread as shell/Ruby backtick execution, an example placeholder URL, and REST/OpenAPI documentation snippets misread as system reconnaissance. There is no executable code, no network activity, no filesystem or environment access, and no prompt-injection content. The skill is safe.

content.user_title: Design Clean REST and GraphQL APIs
content.value_statement: Designing consistent APIs from scratch is slow and error-prone, and inconsistent endpoints confuse consumers. This skill gives Claude a structured workflow with proven patterns for endpoints, errors, versioning, authentication, and OpenAPI documentation.
actual_capabilities: Designs resource-based REST endpoints using nouns and correct HTTP methods
Recommends appropriate HTTP status codes for each operation and error case
Defines consistent success, list-pagination, and error response formats
Advises on URL and header versioning strategies for APIs
Documents authentication patterns such as JWT bearer tokens and API keys
Produces OpenAPI 3.0 specification templates from a provided starting point
limitations: Provides design guidance and documentation only; it does not implement or run API code
Does not test, deploy, or validate a live API against a running server
Covers REST and GraphQL patterns but not every protocol such as gRPC or SOAP
Security advice is general guidance and does not replace a full security review

use_cases.title: Design a new REST API from scratch
use_cases.description: A backend developer uses the skill to structure endpoints, pick status codes, and define request and response formats for a new service.

use_cases.title: Review an existing API contract
use_cases.description: A tech lead asks the skill to check an API against the validation checklist for consistency, correct methods, and pagination.

use_cases.title: Write an OpenAPI specification
use_cases.description: An API documentation writer uses the OpenAPI template to produce a complete and valid specification for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Design endpoints for a resource
prompt_templates.prompt: Design REST endpoints for managing a 'products' resource. Include list, get, create, update, and delete operations with the correct HTTP methods and status codes.

prompt_templates.title: Define response formats
prompt_templates.prompt: Define consistent JSON success, paginated list, and error response formats for my user management API.

prompt_templates.title: Plan versioning and authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a versioning strategy and an authentication pattern for a public API that will have external consumers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing an API for external use

prompt_templates.title: Produce an OpenAPI specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete OpenAPI 3.0 specification for an orders API with endpoints for listing, creating, and retrieving orders, including request bodies, responses, and schemas.
prompt_templates.scenario: Documenting a designed API in full

output_examples.input: Design REST endpoints for a users resource.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a resource-based route set: GET /users to list users, GET /users/{id} to fetch one, POST /users to create, PUT and PATCH /users/{id} to replace or update, and DELETE /users/{id} to remove. Each route is paired with the recommended HTTP status code.

output_examples.input: What status codes should my error responses use?
output_examples.output: The skill explains that 400 signals bad input, 401 signals missing or invalid authentication, 403 signals a permission problem, 404 signals a missing resource, 409 signals a conflict, 422 signals a validation failure, and 429 signals rate limiting.

output_examples.input: How should I version my public API?
output_examples.output: The skill recommends URL versioning such as /api/v1/users as the primary approach and describes header versioning with an Accept header as an alternative for teams that prefer it.

best_practices: Use resource-based URLs with nouns and match HTTP methods to operations.
Keep response formats consistent across every endpoint, including errors.
Document the design with a complete OpenAPI specification before implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not put verbs in URLs, such as /getUser or /createUser.
Do not return the same 200 status code for every response regardless of outcome.
Do not place sensitive data such as tokens or passwords in URLs or query strings.

faq.question: Does this skill write the API code for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, patterns, and documentation. You still implement the API in your chosen language and framework.

faq.question: Does it support both REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes REST endpoint patterns and GraphQL schema design examples with queries, mutations, and types.

faq.question: Which versioning strategy does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends URL versioning such as /api/v1/users as the primary approach and describes header versioning as an alternative.

faq.question: Can it help me write an OpenAPI specification?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides an OpenAPI 3.0 template as a starting point and helps you complete it for your endpoints.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents common patterns including JWT bearer tokens and API keys, and includes a general security checklist.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: Yes. It is a static Markdown reference guide with no executable code, no network activity, and no file or environment access.
